incidents.victim: Apollo Global Management
incidents.vector: Voice-phishing and social engineering in which attackers impersonated IT support to gain access to the firm's cloud platforms.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed cloud systems July 6-10 and stole names, dates of birth, contact details, home addresses and Social Security numbers; Apollo is the first confirmed victim of a broader BlackFile/'The Com'-linked campaign hitting private equity, law and ratings firms.

incidents.victim: U.S. Bancorp (U.S. Bank)
incidents.vector: Breach of a contractor to one of the bank's third-party vendors — a 'fourth-party' incident outside the bank's own environment.
incidents.impact: The LockBit ransomware gang listed the 7th-largest U.S. bank and threatened to leak data; U.S. Bancorp says its own systems, networks and data were not compromised and has referred the matter to law enforcement.

incidents.victim: Windows and Linux web servers (government, education, media, technology, gaming)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of known one-day vulnerabilities (Zimbra, Nacos, AjaxPro) using agentic AI to automate exploitation, reconnaissance and payload generation, then deployment of the SPECTRE cross-platform implant with Linux rootkit and BYOVD EDR-killing capabilities.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos tracked Chinese-speaking crime group UAT-10147 running SEO fraud and data theft against servers in Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam; a target list of ~170,000 URLs was recovered, marking an escalation toward semi-autonomous AI-orchestrated intrusions.

incidents.victim: Academics, aerospace/defense, government and think-tank personnel (Europe and U.S.)
incidents.vector: Persistent social-engineering campaigns abusing legitimate authentication flows — app-password phishing, OAuth and device-code phishing, and WhatsApp device-linking — to bypass MFA and hijack personal accounts.
incidents.impact: Google's Threat Intelligence Group detailed three Russian espionage clusters (including UNC6293/ICE RELIC, formerly APT29, plus UNC7005 and UNC5976) compromising accounts of individuals of interest to the Russian state across multiple platforms.

incidents.victim: Afghan government and telecom organizations; Indian government targets
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with lures impersonating telecom and government tools, delivering the new Patchcord and Sheetcord backdoors; persistence via browser-shortcut hijacking and Google Sheets used for covert command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Acronis tied Transparent Tribe (APT36) to a refreshed toolset that successfully compromised an Afghan Telecom (AFTEL) IT officer and an Afghan subsidiary of an international company; parallel attacks on Indian defense and government agencies have not been confirmed successful.

incidents.victim: Banking customers in Mexico (and some in North America/Europe)
incidents.vector: Spam email delivering a zip archive disguised as an invoice, using DLL sideloading through a legitimate file-management app (Duplicate Files Finder) with extensive anti-analysis and anti-forensics checks.
incidents.impact: Acronis reported a new Grandoreiro banking-trojan campaign, showing the malware remains active more than two years after a 2024 law-enforcement takedown, with a heavily obfuscated loader that steals banking credentials and enables remote control of infected devices.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure operators (water, energy, chemical, manufacturing, food/agriculture, commercial facilities)
incidents.vector: Internet scanning to find exposed Siemens S7 Series PLCs, then AI-generated Python exploit scripts using the snap7 library, disguised as legitimate OT monitoring tools, to gain read/write access via the S7comm protocol.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warned of an 'active threat' conducting reconnaissance and capability development against S7-200/300/400/1200/1500 controllers — assessed as pre-positioning for future operational effects on critical infrastructure; agencies did not attribute the activity but noted a wider PLC-targeting landscape including recent Iran-linked activity against water utilities.

incidents.victim: Government bodies across Central Asia (Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Georgia)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with regionally tailored Office documents (some in password-protected RAR archives) that launch a macro chain deploying remote access trojans; command channels hidden inside legitimate services such as Google Drive.
incidents.impact: Bitdefender detailed 'SilkParasite,' a China-nexus operation (linked to FamousSparrow) using seven RAT families — five previously undocumented and showing AI-assisted development — to establish long-term access to government economic-decision bodies, reflecting China's growing intelligence focus as Russian influence recedes in the region.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government agencies (Ministry of Digital Affairs)
incidents.vector: A multi-agent AI framework built on OpenClaw and Hermes agentic frameworks using up to eight coordinated sub-agents to autonomously run reconnaissance, crack credentials, find and exploit vulnerabilities, exfiltrate records and install backdoors.
incidents.impact: Sovereign AI firm Dream documented what it calls the first 'near-autonomous' AI attack on a nation-state; over 12 attack waves against government web applications during July 1-4, with Taiwan's MODA confirming abnormal AI-driven attacks on government agencies detected in July.

incidents.victim: PTC Windchill / FlexPLM customers (manufacturing, aerospace, automotive — incl. GE, Philips, Shell, Toast, Zebra)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of an unauthenticated remote-code-execution zero-day (CVE-2026-12569) in PTC's Windchill and FlexPLM products, using a custom Windchill-tailored web shell for credential theft and large-scale data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: The Clop extortion group began emailing victims in mid-July claiming data theft from dozens of organizations, including some of the world's largest public companies; the campaign follows Clop's pattern of mass-exploiting SaaS/supply-chain platforms, with impact still emerging.

incidents.victim: CareCloud (electronic health record provider)
incidents.vector: A hacker gained access to one of CareCloud's AWS environments and exfiltrated data over roughly eight hours (March 10-16).
incidents.impact: CareCloud told regulators that 3.76 million people were affected, with stolen data including Social Security numbers, ID numbers, credit/debit card details, medical information and insurance data; no group has claimed responsibility.

incidents.victim: Latvia Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a vulnerability in an internet-facing CSDD system where several mandatory cybersecurity requirements had not been met.
incidents.impact: A targeted attack exposed payment-receipt data dating to 2008 for more than 1.2 million people (about two-thirds of Latvia's population) and 200,000 businesses; the incident escalated into a political crisis, with the agency's supervisory board resigning and its chief preparing to step down.

incidents.victim: Slovakia national traffic-camera network
incidents.vector: Hardware supply-chain compromise — NERO R-ONE speed cameras (a rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M model) contain a backdoor that grants shell and network access via SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers, with SecureBoot disabled and unauthenticated exposed video streams.
incidents.impact: Slovakia's national security service NBU flagged 279 cameras, bought through a Cyprus shell company under a €30M EU-funded project, as containing a Russian backdoor; deployment was paused pending an independent audit, and similar devices are reportedly installed elsewhere in Eastern Europe.

incidents.victim: Winnipeg Health Sciences Centre (Canada)
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack affecting building-management and access-control systems.
incidents.impact: The attack disabled access-control doors and HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) at Manitoba's largest hospital, forcing increased on-site security while the access-card system remained down; the hospital said patient care and clinical operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: Berlin city government (Germany)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed vector against two municipal departments.
incidents.impact: The attack took down emails, remote gateways and internet connectivity across the transport and urban-development departments; IT staff disconnected both agencies from the city network to contain the incident.

incidents.victim: Ukraine ARMA (agency for managing seized Russian assets)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed vector, unattributed by the agency.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted ARMA's operations just as it was preparing to assign a new manager for a beverage company seized from an Alfa-Bank co-founder after Russia's invasion; timing suggests a link to that asset dispute.

incidents.victim: Rust software ecosystem (Arrayref and two other libraries)
incidents.vector: Compromise of a popular Rust developer's account to inject malware into three of their libraries, including Arrayref (~5 million weekly downloads).
incidents.impact: The malicious versions were live for only 23 minutes before the Rust security team removed them and locked the account; Wiz linked the attacker infrastructure to North Korean operations, underscoring continued DPRK supply-chain targeting of developers.

incidents.victim: BlueSky and GitHub
incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) flooding attacks.
incidents.impact: An Iranian hacktivist group calling itself the 313 Team took down BlueSky and GitHub in consecutive attacks over Sunday and Monday, causing prolonged outages; the same group ran a prior DDoS wave in April.

incidents.victim: 1,100+ companies hiring remote technical staff (software, staffing, healthcare, financial sectors)
incidents.vector: Fraudulent employment operations using at least 22 fabricated personas, AI-generated profile photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and real-time AI transcription to pass interviews and secure remote jobs, with facilitators maintaining company-issued hardware.
incidents.impact: Recorded Future's Insikt Group detailed 'PurpleDelta' North Korean IT-worker clusters (operators likely based in China) that applied to over 1,100 companies and were likely actively employed at ten or more, funneling earnings to the North Korean regime while posing an insider-threat and downstream-compromise risk.

incidents.victim: 500+ organizations across healthcare, education, legal, insurance, technology and manufacturing
incidents.vector: Recruitment of initial access brokers plus exploitation of unpatched software (e.g. ScreenConnect, Fortinet EMS, Fortra GoAnywhere, BeyondTrust CVE-2026-1731) — often weaponizing new CVEs within 24 hours — followed by double-extortion.
incidents.impact: An updated FBI/CISA/HHS advisory reports the Medusa ransomware-as-a-service operation has now impacted over 500 victims through April 2026, encrypting data and threatening to leak exfiltrated files, with healthcare a frequent target.

incidents.victim: On-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server operators
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of multiple SharePoint Server vulnerabilities (including newly added CVE-2026-55040) to achieve remote code execution, then theft of IIS machine keys and deserialization techniques for persistence and malware deployment.
incidents.impact: CISA updated its alert urging all supported on-premises SharePoint versions (Subscription Edition, 2019, 2016) to patch and harden after continued exploitation enabling unauthorized access and persistence.

incidents.victim: Government, critical infrastructure and other organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: Initial access chiefly via exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN and firewall appliances (e.g. FortiOS/FortiProxy CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-24472), followed by double-extortion.
incidents.impact: A joint FBI/CISA/NSA/DC3/USSS/Korean National Police advisory warned of Gunra, a Conti-derived ransomware-as-a-service that expanded to an affiliate model in 2026, encrypting data and threatening to publish stolen files across victims in the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
